title: Field Origination Triage Worksheet — enterprise request consolidation and initial-scope heuristic
creator: Priya Nair
description: Purpose: Provide a compact, repeatable worksheet that CS/Sales can use to consolidate high-touch enterprise feature asks, produce a first-pass technical and economic scope, and route items to the right PM/engineering path. This ticket creates the canonical worksheet, scoring heuristic, and the handoff rules for immediate next steps (prototype, spike, RFC, or backlog).
problem_statement: Sales and CS frequently surface feature asks during renewal and pilot conversations. We lack a short, consistent way to: (1) consolidate multiple account asks, (2) estimate engineering scope and unit economics quickly, and (3) decide an operational path (fast-track prototype vs. multi-sprint program). Result: long triage cycles, duplicated PM triage work, and missed enterprise motions.
objectives: Ship a one-page worksheet (Confluence + Google Sheet template) used by CS/Sales to capture the minimal fields required for a first-pass scope
Define a 5-metric scoring heuristic (Value, Effort, Risk/Compliance, Strategic Alignment, Volume) with weights and thresholds
Add routing rules that map scores to next steps (Prototype/Spike/RFC/Backlog) and required approvals
Integrate with existing ticketing (HubSpot -> Linear) and surface key fields in the Linear ticket for PMs
worksheet_fields: Customer & Account Context (ARR, renewal date, contact)
Success criteria / KPIs (how customer will measure success)
Approx monthly usage signal (tokens/requests) or expected integration volume
Integration complexity (outbound webhooks, SSO, data residency, connectors)
Compliance constraints (PII, regulated industry, data residency required)
High-level engineering scope estimate (S, M, L, XL) with assumptions
Suggested economic model (per-seat, per-token, fixed-add-on) and price sensitivity
Strategic rationale (account expansion, logo, referenceable case study)
Attachments / links (Drive PRD, demo video, HubSpot thread)
scoring_rubric: Five metrics, 1-5 each. Weights: Value(0.35), Effort(0.25), Risk/Compliance(0.15), Strategic Alignment(0.15), Volume(0.10). Score = weighted sum. Thresholds: >=3.8 -> Green(Prototype / fast-track), 3.0-3.79 -> Yellow(Scoped spike + PM review), <3.0 -> Red(Backlog unless strategic override).
routing_rules: Green: assign PM + engineering partner, create Spike (2 week proto) and commit to customer demo in 4 weeks
Yellow: create technical spike + cost estimate, escalate to Eng manager for feasibility clearance
Red: capture as backlog item, offer product workaround or roadmap askback; if account asks exceed $100k ARR or is legal/regulatory, escalate regardless of score
Compliance: if 'data residency' or 'regulated industry' is flagged, attach legal review step and mark Risk/Compliance score minimum 3
acceptance_criteria: Worksheet published in Confluence with editable Google Sheet template
Integration mapping documented for HubSpot -> Linear that populates key fields in new Linear ticket
Scoring heuristic validated on 10 recent enterprise asks (retro exercise) and thresholds adjusted
CS playbook updated with 3 example filled worksheets and decision flowchart
PMs can reliably decide next step within 48 hours after worksheet submission
decisions_made: Keep worksheet to a single page to ensure adoption
Use weighted 1-5 scoring; weights set to prioritize customer value and engineering effort
Require Legal for any asks that implicate data residency or >$250k potential annual contract impact
Automate HubSpot->Linear mapping to reduce PM copy/paste friction
tradeoffs_and_considerations: Speed vs fidelity: keeping worksheet lightweight increases velocity but will surface unknowns later; mitigated by mandatory spike when Effort>3
Standardization vs account-specific customization: template must be generic but include a freeform 'constraints' field for special requirements
Signal quality: scoring depends on accurate volume estimates from CS — we'll provide a short lookup guide to convert customer language into token/requests estimates
